cases.sentence: В средине моста, слезши с лошади, прижатый своим ___ к перилам, стоял князь Несвицкий.
cases.explain: «толстым телом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Two of the enemy’s shots had already flown across the bridge, where there was a crush. Halfway across stood Prince Nesvítski, who had alighted from his horse and whose big body was jammed against the railings. He looked back laughing to the Cossack who stood a few steps behind him holding two horses by their bridles. Each time Prince Nesvítski tried to move on, soldiers and carts pushed him back again and pressed him against the railings, and all he could do was to smile.

cases.sentence: — говорил казак ___ с повозкой, напиравшему на толпившуюся у самых колес и лошадей пехоту, — экой ты!
cases.explain: «фурштатскому солдату» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “What a fine fellow you are, friend!” said the Cossack to a convoy soldier with a wagon, who was pressing onto the infantrymen who were crowded together close to his wheels and his horses. “What a fellow! You can’t wait a moment! Don’t you see the general wants to pass?”

cases.sentence: — Как он (он — неприятель) таперича по мосту примется зажаривать, — говорил мрачно ___, обращаясь к товарищу, — забудешь чесаться.
cases.explain: «старый солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “If he” (“he” meant the enemy) “begins popping at the bridge now,” said the old soldier dismally to a comrade, “you’ll forget to scratch yourself.”

cases.sentence: За ним ___ ехал на повозке.
cases.explain: «другой солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: That soldier passed on, and after him came another sitting on a cart.

cases.sentence: — Как он его, ___, полыхнет прикладом-то в самые зубы...
cases.explain: «милый человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And then, old fellow, he gives him one in the teeth with the butt end of his gun …” a soldier whose greatcoat was well tucked up said gaily, with a wide swing of his arm.

cases.sentence: — Как он его, милый человек, полыхнет прикладом-то в ___...
cases.explain: «самые зубы» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “And then, old fellow, he gives him one in the teeth with the butt end of his gun …” a soldier whose greatcoat was well tucked up said gaily, with a wide swing of his arm.

cases.sentence: — То-то оно, ___, — отвечал другой с хохотом.
cases.explain: «сладкая ветчина-то» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, the ham was just delicious …” answered another with a loud laugh. And they, too, passed on, so that Nesvítski did not learn who had been struck on the teeth, or what the ham had to do with it.

cases.sentence: — Как оно пролетит мимо меня, дяденька, ядро-то, — говорил, едва удерживаясь от смеха, с ___ молодой солдат, — я так и обмер.
cases.explain: «огромным ртом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “As it flies past me, Daddy, the ball I mean,” said a young soldier with an enormous mouth, hardly refraining from laughing, “I felt like dying of fright. I did, ’pon my word, I got that frightened!” said he, as if bragging of having been frightened.

cases.sentence: — Как оно пролетит мимо меня, дяденька, ядро-то, — говорил, едва удерживаясь от смеха, с огромным ртом ___, — я так и обмер.
cases.explain: «молодой солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “As it flies past me, Daddy, the ball I mean,” said a young soldier with an enormous mouth, hardly refraining from laughing, “I felt like dying of fright. I did, ’pon my word, I got that frightened!” said he, as if bragging of having been frightened.

cases.sentence: Это был ___ на паре, нагруженный, казалось, целым домом; за форшпаном, который вез немец, привязана была красивая, пестрая, с огромным вымем, корова.
cases.explain: «немецкий форшпан» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: That one also passed. Then followed a cart unlike any that had gone before. It was a German cart with a pair of horses led by a German, and seemed loaded with a whole houseful of effects. A fine brindled cow with a large udder was attached to the cart behind. A woman with an unweaned baby, an old woman, and a healthy German girl with bright red cheeks were sitting on some feather beds. Evidently these fugitives were allowed to pass by special permission. The eyes of all the soldiers turned toward the women, and while the vehicle was passing at foot pace all the soldiers’ remarks related to the two young ones. Every face bore almost the same smile, expressing unseemly thoughts about the women.

cases.sentence: Это был немецкий форшпан на паре, нагруженный, казалось, ___; за форшпаном, который вез немец, привязана была красивая, пестрая, с огромным вымем, корова.

cases.sentence: — Продай матушку̀, — ударяя на ___, говорил другой солдат, обращаясь к немцу, который, опустив глаза, сердито и испуганно шел широким шагом.
cases.explain: «последнем слоге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Sell me the missis,” said another soldier, addressing the German, who, angry and frightened, strode energetically along with downcast eyes. “See how smart she’s made herself! Oh, the devils!”

cases.sentence: — Продай матушку̀, — ударяя на последнем слоге, говорил ___, обращаясь к немцу, который, опустив глаза, сердито и испуганно шел широким шагом.

cases.sentence: Как это часто бывает, на выезде моста замялись лошади в ___, и вся толпа должна была ждать.
cases.explain: «ротной повозке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The girl smiled and took it. Nesvítski like the rest of the men on the bridge did not take his eyes off the women till they had passed. When they had gone by, the same stream of soldiers followed, with the same kind of talk, and at last all stopped. As often happens, the horses of a convoy wagon became restive at the end of the bridge, and the whole crowd had to wait.

cases.sentence: Вишь, и офицера-то приперли, — говорили с ___ остановившиеся толпы, оглядывая друг друга, и всё жались вперед к выходу.
cases.explain: «разных сторон» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “And why are they stopping? There’s no proper order!” said the soldiers. “Where are you shoving to? Devil take you! Can’t you wait? It’ll be worse if he fires the bridge. See, here’s an officer jammed in too”—different voices were saying in the crowd, as the men looked at one another, and all pressed toward the exit from the bridge.

cases.sentence: Он с ___ добрался до лошади.
cases.explain: «большим усилием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: With great difficulty he managed to get to his horse, and shouting continually he moved on. The soldiers squeezed themselves to make way for him, but again pressed on him so that they jammed his leg, and those nearest him were not to blame for they were themselves pressed still harder from behind.

cases.sentence: Солдаты с ___ нажались друг на друга, и Денисов присоединился к Несвицкому.
cases.explain: «испуганными лицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The soldiers crowded against one another with terrified faces, and Denísov joined Nesvítski.

cases.sentence: — ___ то туда, то сюда таскают полк.
cases.explain: «Целый день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “They don’t even give one time to dwink!” answered Váska Denísov. “They keep dwagging the wegiment to and fwo all day. If they mean to fight, let’s fight. But the devil knows what this is.”

cases.sentence: — оглядывая его ___ и вальтрап, сказал Несвицкий.
cases.explain: «новый ментик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What a dandy you are today!” said Nesvítski, looking at Denísov’s new cloak and saddlecloth.

cases.sentence: ___ Несвицкого, сопровождаемая казаком, и решительность Денисова, махавшего саблею и отчаянно кричавшего, подействовали так, что они протискались на ту сторону моста и остановили пехоту.
cases.explain: «Осанистая фигура» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The imposing figure of Nesvítski followed by his Cossack, and the determination of Denísov who flourished his sword and shouted frantically, had such an effect that they managed to squeeze through to the farther side of the bridge and stopped the infantry. Beside the bridge Nesvítski found the colonel to whom he had to deliver the order, and having done this he rode back.

cases.sentence: По доскам моста раздались ___ копыт, как будто скакало несколько лошадей, и эскадрон, с офицерами впереди, по четыре человека в ряд, растянулся по мосту и стал выходить на ту сторону.
cases.explain: «прозрачные звуки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Having cleared the way Denísov stopped at the end of the bridge. Carelessly holding in his stallion that was neighing and pawing the ground, eager to rejoin its fellows, he watched his squadron draw nearer. Then the clang of hoofs, as of several horses galloping, resounded on the planks of the bridge, and the squadron, officers in front and men four abreast, spread across the bridge and began to emerge on his side of it.
